title: Eli: a drill checkpoint reached through the wrong movement
publisher: Dom Caminiti | Golf Swing Reviews / domcaminitigolf

context.format: Review of an existing student drill attempt with coach correction demonstration

coverage.transcript_kind: Local MLX Whisper ASR with visual inspection
coverage.visual_review_method: 15 overview and 34 detail frames across five portrait sheets inspected; student drill attempt, hand-height boxes and coach hinge demonstration reviewed.
limitations: Coach reasoning is attributed, not independently validated.

evidence.attribution: Dom Caminiti | Golf Swing Reviews / domcaminitigolf
evidence.session: Eli: a drill checkpoint reached through the wrong movement
evidence.summary: Eli has begun a drill using stick extended along club shaft, initially prescribed because club went too low/inside. Coach sees improvement in club staying in front of hands and stick running down lead leg. Prior inside takeaway is reported history; current footage shows drill attempt.

frames.observation: Stick extends from club grip toward lead leg.

limitations: 2D annotated footage; no independent causal validation.

evidence.attribution: Dom Caminiti | Golf Swing Reviews / domcaminitigolf
evidence.session: Eli: a drill checkpoint reached through the wrong movement
evidence.summary: Coach questions how checkpoint was reached: student lifts hands above starting hand-height box to bring clubhead level, rather than hinge club while hands stay low. Desired arrows illustrate separate hand and clubhead actions.
limitations: 2D annotated footage; no independent causal validation.

evidence.attribution: Dom Caminiti | Golf Swing Reviews / domcaminitigolf
evidence.session: Eli: a drill checkpoint reached through the wrong movement
evidence.summary: Coach demonstrates starting with turn, arms/hands following inside hand-plane line, and gradual vertical wrist hinge. Hand box shows his hands slightly lower during takeaway while club rises to hand height, running extended stick down lead leg.

frames.observation: Hands move down/in relative to box.

limitations: 2D annotated footage; no independent causal validation.

evidence.attribution: Dom Caminiti | Golf Swing Reviews / domcaminitigolf
evidence.session: Eli: a drill checkpoint reached through the wrong movement
evidence.summary: Coach claims hinge stores more energy/leverage for later release and that golfers without it often lift arms and over-rotate/spin body from top to search for speed. These are unmeasured explanatory claims, not a diagnosis proved from Eli's rehearsal. No post-correction Eli shot is shown.

frames.observation: Illustrative release arrow over original student drill.

limitations: 2D annotated footage; no independent causal validation.

cases.title: Correct hand lifting within the shaft-stick takeaway drill
cases.coaching_finding: Student reaches stick-down-leg and clubhead-at-hand-height checkpoint partly by lifting hands.
cases.coach_reasoning: Coach distinguishes the endpoint from its mechanism: desired clubhead rise comes from wrist hinge while turn carries relatively low hands inward.

intervention.setup: Extend alignment stick along club shaft; source mentions seven iron but says other clubs can be used.
intervention.cue: Let turn carry hands inward and low while gradually hinging club up.
intervention.check: Compare hands with their starting-height box, as well as stick/leg contact and clubhead height.
intervention.limits: No repetitions, shaft flex or energy measurement supplied.

applicability: Assess a golfer actually doing this drill; reaching the prop checkpoint alone is insufficient.
Use comparable camera framing and starting hand reference.
Hands low is a takeaway instruction, not a command to keep them low at top.
unknowns: Exact grip/attachment setup and original undrilled baseline.
Mechanical energy, speed and generalized spin-out causal claim.
cases.observed_result: Partial existing drill success identified, correction demonstrated by coach; no Eli retest or measured performance change.

selection.coaching_focus: One takeaway mechanism within existing drill
selection.policy_origin: User one-focus preference; retain source sequencing and avoid simultaneous competing thoughts.
selection.reassess: Proposed app check: review hand-height path and club rise together, then verify aid-free strike instead of merely checking stick contact.

measurement_register.value: Student hands rise out of starting box; coach hands stay low/slightly lower as club rises
Hinge stores energy/leverage and may avoid speed-seeking spin-out
limits: No force, shaft deflection, energy or speed measurement; not an automatic downstream diagnosis.

cross_source_links.explanation: Clapp distinguishes timing of forearm rotation; Dom here distinguishes wrist hinge from hand lift. Club position alone cannot identify which component produced it.

cross_source_links.relation: Drill success requires more than apparent compliance
cross_source_links.explanation: Ruffels checks aid-free target execution. Eli also shows why a prop checkpoint needs mechanism inspection before it is called successful practice.

annotation_opportunities: Track start hand box and clubhead height together.
Show actual student attempt beside coach demonstration, labelled separately.
Avoid numerical stored-energy claims from 2D geometry.
excluded_material: Generalized body spin claim treated as observed Eli fault.

independent_validation.reason: Source extraction preserves evidence and conditions; a source match and response check are still needed for another golfer.
